newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.LANKA RUPEE ENDS UP AMID LOW DEMAND.
newsitem.headline: S.LANKA RUPEE ENDS UP AMID LOW DEMAND.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee closed higher against the dollar on Tuesday due to low rupee demand and high dollar supply, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 58.91 to the dollar after opening at 58.93, they said.
"There was little interest in dollars, which were also well supplied," said a Commercial Bank dealer. "Low interest in dollars was due to a lack of imports and high call rates."
Overnight call money closed at 13.0 percent after opening at 10.5 and rising to 13.5, dealers said.

"Money is a bit tight because some banks have invested in the secondary Treasury bill market," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer."But the tightness should ease soon because banks are selling dollars to the central bank."
The central bank pushed up the dollar by half a local cent, fixing buying and selling prices at 59.9100 and 60.1001, respectively.
